chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari narrated from Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, who said: I was with Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) when permission was sought for a man from Yemen. A tall, robust man entered and greeted him with 'al-Wilayah'. I said to myself: Who is this man?

Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: He is from the offspring of the Bedouin lady, the owner of the pebble, upon which my ancestors had their seals impressed, and they were imprinted. Then he said: Bring it here. He brought out a pebble, and on one side there was a smooth spot. The Imam placed his seal on it, and it was imprinted. As if I could read the inscription of his seal at this very moment: Al-Hasan ibn Ali.

Then the man rose while saying: 'May the mercy and blessings of Allah be upon you, O People of the House.' 'Progeny, some of which from others.' I testify that your right is the obligatory right, like the obligation of the right of Amir al-Mu'minin and the Imams (peace be upon them). To you has ended wisdom and Wilayah, and you are the Wali of Allah, in whom no one has an excuse of ignorance.

I asked him about his name, and he said: My name is Mahja' ibn al-Salt ibn Uqbah ibn Sim'an ibn Ghanam ibn Umm Ghanam. And she is the Yemeni Bedouin lady, the owner of the pebble upon which Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) sealed... The end of the hadith.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْت: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Who is the Yemeni visitor in the hadith of Imam Hasan al-Askari and what is the significance of the pebble?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the physical continuity of Imamate through the 'pebble of the Bedouin woman,' a tangible symbol of authority passed down from Imam Ali (a.s.) to Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). The narrative underscores the concept of *Nass* (designation) and the hereditary nature of Wilayah, as the visitor explicitly links the Imam’s authority to that of the Prophet’s household, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of the infallible Imam’s obligatory recognition.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 171 - Saad bin Abdullah Ashari has narrated from Abu Hashim Dawood bin Qasim Ja’fari that he said: I was with Imam Hasan Askari (a.s) when permission for entry was sought for a Yemenite gentleman. When he entered, we saw that he was tall and he greeted the Imam as the owner of authority. I said to myself: If I only knew who this man is!

Imam (a.s) said: He is the descendant of the Bedouin lady who possessed the pebble on which my ancestors had placed their seals. After that the Imam (a.s) said: Show that pebble, and he brought it out. The Imam placed his seal on the part, which was empty. As if we can still read the seal of the Imam and print of His Eminence that he had written: Hasan bin Ali.

After that the man arose and said: Peace and blessings of Allah be on you, O Ahle Bayt (a.s); progeny in which some have emerged from others. I testify that your right, like the right of Amirul Momineen (a.s) and the Holy Imams (a.s) is obligatory; wisdom and Wilayat ends at you. You are the Wali (divine saint) of God and no one can offer any excuse of ignorance about you.

I asked him what his name was; and he replied: My name is Mahja bin Salat bin Uqbah bin Samaan bin Ghanam bin Umme Ghanam. And she is the Bedouin lady from Yemen, owner of the pebble for whom Amirul Momineen (a.s) placed his seal (on the pebble).
